title: Finite derived pullback and normalized slice cohomology restriction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $X,U$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $u:U\to X$ be an object of the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; in particular $u$ is weakly etale. Use the site identification $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and the constant-ring identification $A_U\simeq A_X|_U$ of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $R_U$ be the exact module restriction functor of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], transported to $A_U$-modules by this ring identification. Thus $(R_UF)(W\to U)=F(W\to X)$ with its restricted action. Write $D(R_U)$ for its termwise induced functor on the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $Lu^*$ for the finite-level canonical derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], using the specified coefficient structure map of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

There is a natural isomorphism $\eta:Lu^*\xrightarrow{\sim}D(R_U)$ whose component on any representative cochain complex is induced degreewise by the graph-coprojection module comparison of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], with the canonical coefficient map fixing constant sections. For each $r\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$c^r_K:\mathcal H^r(Lu^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_U(\mathcal H^rK),\qquad K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A),$$
where cohomology sheaves are those of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. On representatives, $c^r$ is induced by $\eta$ and the restriction identifications of cycles and boundaries, with the canonical maps from cycles to cohomology. For every derived morphism $\psi:K\to L$ (including morphisms represented by roofs),
$$c^r_L\circ\mathcal H^r(Lu^*\psi)=R_U(\mathcal H^r\psi)\circ c^r_K.$$

source.place: Tag 03CE, label lemma-localize-given-products, in its derived constant-coefficient module form; homology.tex lemma-exact-functor and derived.tex lemma-right-derived-exact-functor give the cohomology and termwise localization comparisons. proof.text: Put $F=u^*$ on module sheaves and $R=R_U$, and use right-to-left composition. Apply clauses (1)-(3) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] with $r=u$ and $W=U$. The hypothesis is exactly that $u$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$; no surjectivity or open-immersion hypothesis is needed. They give the graph-coprojection isomorphism $b:F\xrightarrow{\sim}R$, natural in module sheaves. Clause (2), with [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](2)-(3), identifies the specified structure map with the inverse of $A_U\to A_X|_U$ fixing constant sections. Thus this is the required $A_U$-linear comparison, with precisely the ring transport in the statement. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], restriction to the slice is exact. Transport through the site equivalence and the ring isomorphism preserves exact sequences (each transport has an inverse), so $R$ is exact; $F\cong R$ is exact as well. Both functors are additive: restriction adds maps sectionwise, and $b$ transfers that equality to $F$.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; module form: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero (restriction $j_U^*$ of module sheaves and its left adjoint). The graph and coefficient normalization are the cited object-inverse-image-restriction statement.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for $F$ and $R$. Write $Q_X,Q_U$ for the localization functors and $a_T:D(T)Q_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_UC(T)$ for the factorizations, where $T=F,R$ and $C(T)$ means termwise application. Both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. By the unbounded clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], $D(F)$ with this factorization is the left derived functor of $F$. The finite-level $Lu^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is that of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: the functor induced termwise by this same $F$, same coefficient map. The uniqueness of that derived functor therefore gives the counit-compatible isomorphism $\lambda:Lu^*\xrightarrow{\sim}D(F)$. Its normalization can also be read directly on a K-flat resolution $q:P\to K$: the computation map is induced by $F(q):C(F)P\to C(F)K$, a quasi-isomorphism because $F$ is exact. Hence under $\lambda$ every representative $K$ computes $Lu^*K$ by $C(F)K$, as specified in the finite-level definition. No bound on $K$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, unbounded assertion and dual left-derived assertion; finite-level K-flat computation in the cited derived-pullback definition.

proof.text:
Naturality of $b$ at every differential gives $R(d^i)b_{K^i}=b_{K^{i+1}}F(d^i)$, so its degreewise components define an isomorphism of complexes $C(b)_K:C(F)K\to C(R)K$. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] to these exact functors and $b$. It gives $D(b):D(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(R)$ with normalization
$$a_{R,K}D(b)_{Q_XK}=Q_U(C(b)_K)a_{F,K}.$$
Set $\eta=D(b)\lambda$. This proves the required natural isomorphism and its degreewise graph normalization. In particular a resolution does not change this normalization: naturality at $q:P\to K$ gives $C(R)(q)C(b)_P=C(b)_KC(F)(q)$; after inverting the two quasi-isomorphisms, the comparison computed from $P$ is exactly the one induced by $C(b)_K$. The coefficients remain those fixed in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural-isomorphism enhancement: Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean, liftNatIso, as recorded in the cited node.

proof.text:
Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact functor $R$. It supplies a natural isomorphism on complexes
$$\gamma^r_K:H^r(C(R)K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R(H^rK).$$
Its statement identifies $\ker R(d^r)$ with $R(\ker d^r)$ and $\operatorname{im}R(d^{r-1})$ with $R(\operatorname{im}d^{r-1})$, and specifies compatibility with the cycle inclusion and the projection onto cohomology. Thus $\gamma^r$ is the required normalized restriction map on the quotient of cycles by boundaries, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of those objects. By [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], these are the cohomology sheaves of the represented objects, with quotient in the abelian category of module sheaves. This argument uses exactness, not the generally false assertion that evaluating a sheaf complex on an object computes its sheaf cohomology.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied to cycles and boundaries; normalized cochain cohomology comparison in the cited exact-functor-complex-cohomology node.

proof.text:
Use $Q_X$ as the localization at quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The two complex functors $H^rC(R)$ and $RH^r$ invert quasi-isomorphisms: for the former use the preservation in Step 2 and the definition of quasi-isomorphism, and for the latter apply $R$ to the isomorphism $H^r(q)$. Their specified lifts are $\mathcal H^rD(R)$ (using $a_R$) and $R\mathcal H^r$ (using the cohomology factorization of that definition). Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with target the category of $A_U$-module sheaves and with $\tau=\gamma^r$. It yields a natural isomorphism
$$\bar\gamma^r:\mathcal H^rD(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal H^r.$$
The formula in that clause specifies its component on $Q_XK$ as $\gamma^r_K$ under exactly these factorizations. Thus it preserves the cycle-to-cohomology normalization of Step 4 and is natural on all derived morphisms, not only images of chain maps.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; fully faithful precomposition and liftNatIso of Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean:278-361, as recorded in the cited universal-property node.

proof.text:
Define $c^r_K=\bar\gamma^r_K\circ\mathcal H^r(\eta_K)$. Its two factors are isomorphisms by Steps 3 and 5, and Steps 3-4 give the stated representative normalization. For any derived $\psi:K\to L$, naturality of those two factors gives, in order,
$$\begin{aligned}
c^r_L\mathcal H^r(Lu^*\psi)
&=\bar\gamma^r_L\mathcal H^r(D(R)\psi)\mathcal H^r(\eta_K)\\
&=R(\mathcal H^r\psi)\bar\gamma^r_K\mathcal H^r(\eta_K)
=R(\mathcal H^r\psi)c^r_K.
\end{aligned}$$
For a roof $K\xleftarrow{q}P\xrightarrow{f}L$, let $S=\mathcal H^rLu^*$ and $T=R\mathcal H^r$. Naturality at $q$ is $c_KS(q)=T(q)c_P$. Since $q$ is inverted, this implies $c_PS(q)^{-1}=T(q)^{-1}c_K$. Combining with $c_LS(f)=T(f)c_P$ gives $c_LS(f)S(q)^{-1}=T(f)T(q)^{-1}c_K$, precisely the asserted equation for the roof. No choice of a chain-map representative for an arbitrary derived morphism is used.
